claims.text: Q235 steel in the as-received state has a naturally formed thin native oxide film.
As-received Q235 steel contains microstructural heterogeneities such as grain boundaries and inclusions.
The native iron oxide film governs the onset or suppression of corrosion on Q235 steel in harsh chloride-containing environments.
A robust, chemically stable oxide layer suppresses further corrosion.
Mechanical or thermal compromise of the oxide film promotes localized corrosion by exposing active metal sites.
Mild oxidizing annealing will reinforce the native oxide layer on Q235 steel.
Mechanical cleaning will partially remove the native oxide layer.
The relevant structural mediator is the oxide film's chemical composition, thickness, and continuity.
An intact native oxide acts as a passivating barrier that reduces metal dissolution.
Disruption of the oxide barrier accelerates corrosion through enhanced anodic dissolution at exposed sites.
An oxide film reinforced by mild oxidizing annealing will slow degradation.
Relative to untreated Q235 steel, a reinforced, thicker, and more uniform oxide layer will produce lower weight loss.
Relative to untreated Q235 steel, a reinforced oxide layer will produce lower pitting density.
Relative to untreated Q235 steel, a reinforced oxide layer will produce higher electrochemical impedance.
Partial removal or disruption of the oxide film will accelerate corrosion relative to untreated Q235 steel.
The proposed comparison uses untreated, oxidizing-annealed, and mechanically cleaned Q235 samples exposed to 3.5 wt.% NaCl at room temperature and approximately 100°C.
Weight loss, EIS, SEM-based pitting density, and XPS-based oxide characterization can distinguish the proposed corrosion responses and surface mediator.
The hypothesis is limited to low-alloy carbon steels such as Q235 where the native oxide is the primary corrosion-influencing interface.
The proposed mechanism may not transfer to highly alloyed steels or deliberately coated steels.
The cited study investigated corrosion properties of ZrC-containing CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy-alloy coatings deposited on Q235 steel.

contradictions.description: Mechanical cleaning is described as only partially removing the oxide in the intervention, but as removing the oxide in the experimental design; these imply different mediator states.

The conditions state that pretreatment will be the only difference between samples, while the design also varies temperature. This is coherent only if comparisons are made within each temperature regime, which is not stated explicitly.
